title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
summary: Trains a defender to assess intent and commit to an explicit safety decision before responding in multi-turn conversations.
caveat: Reported gains come from the evaluated models and benchmarks; they do not establish resistance to every adaptive attack.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Revisiting Over-refusal in Safety-aligned Large Language Models: A Representation and Optimization Perspective
summary: Analyzes how representation overlap and coupled training gradients can cause benign requests to be refused; proposes a gradient-and-contrastive-learning mitigation.
caveat: The proposed explanation and mitigation need validation beyond the studied model families and benchmarks.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Monitor Accuracy Isn't the Answer: A Decision-Value Framework for Evaluating AI Agent Restart Monitors
summary: Evaluates whether acting on a monitor improves outcomes, rather than treating classification accuracy as sufficient evidence that restarting an agent is useful.
caveat: The restart analysis uses explicit assumptions about remaining budget and replacement attempts; results are not a general proof that monitoring fails.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: SpecGuard: Detecting Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks via Specification-Based Runtime Monitoring
summary: Combines explicit temporal safety specifications with dialogue observations to produce replayable evidence when multi-turn interactions violate a specification.
caveat: Formal checking applies to the represented facts and chosen specification; converting natural language into those facts can still fail.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Alignment of Autonomous Cyber Defense Agents via Adaptive Policy Shaping
summary: Adjusts a trained cyber-defense policy at inference time to reflect changing operational priorities without retraining the whole agent.
caveat: Evaluated in a simulated defense environment; transfer to operational networks is not established by the abstract.
publication_status: Authors report CAMLIS acceptance; venue not independently checked
